You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the orthorhombic space group Ama2, number 40, with Hall symbol A 2 -2a. The input cell is not the conventional symmetry cell: it is a hexagonal-appearing cell with lattice parameters a = b = 6.09129027 Å, c = 10.506523 Å, α = β = 90.0°, and γ = 116.07323532000001°. This input cell contains 16 atoms with the declared composition Eu₂Cu₄Sn₂S₈.

To recover the standard setting from the input fractional coordinates, the relation q_standard = P q_input + s applies, where P is the matrix whose rows are approximately (0, 0, 1), (1/2, −1/2, 0), and (1/2, 1/2, 0), and the origin shift s is effectively zero, with components 0.0, −2.7755575615628914×10⁻¹⁷, and −2.7755575615628914×10⁻¹⁷. Thus the standard c axis corresponds to the input c direction, while the standard a and b axes are obtained from the difference and sum of the input a and b directions, respectively.

In the standard frame, europium occupies the fourfold Wyckoff orbit 4a with coordinate relation (0, 0, z). The representative Eu atom lies at (0, 0, 0.4779169999999999), so the single independent positional parameter is z = 0.4779169999999999. Copper occupies the eightfold general-position orbit 8c with coordinate relation (x, y, z). Its representative position is (0.12604300000000024, 0.21418800000000005, 0.06697400000000009), giving the three independent parameters x = 0.12604300000000024, y = 0.21418800000000005, and z = 0.06697400000000009. Tin occupies a fourfold 4b orbit with coordinate relation (1/4, y, z); the representative Sn atom is at (0.25, 0.3481765, 0.5569635), so y = 0.3481765 and z = 0.5569635.

Sulfur is distributed over three independent orbits. One sulfur sublattice is an eightfold 8c orbit with representative position (0.06794500000000026, 0.2410859999999999, 0.72525), corresponding to x = 0.06794500000000026, y = 0.2410859999999999, and z = 0.72525. The other two sulfur sublattices are distinct fourfold 4b orbits, both of the form (1/4, y, z). The first has representative position (0.25, 0.3996584999999999, 0.18667750000000005), with y = 0.3996584999999999 and z = 0.18667750000000005. The second has representative position (0.25, 0.05872250000000001, 0.23556349999999995), with y = 0.05872250000000001 and z = 0.23556349999999995.

Taken together, these independent orbits generate four Eu atoms, eight Cu atoms, four Sn atoms, and sixteen S atoms in the conventional standard cell, while the supplied input cell contains Eu₂Cu₄Sn₂S₈. No precision corrections are listed; the coordinates are to be understood at the stated rounding precision of six digits where applicable.
